label: early original-phase x/t/3 after a d/u/s/t/p/x/r/y/i prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at positions 1-3 (t=2 alone holds 59% of mass; t=1 and t=3 about 20% each; it never fires at t=0 or in the delimiter/copy phases). The input token matters most: x, t and 3 together hold about 81% of mass (lift 7-8x), and r, y, p, i, h, 1, 2 fire weakly. The preceding tokens set the magnitude: prefixes made of d, u, s, t, p, x, r, y, i raise it, and d does so most strongly. The top activations are d d [x] and d d [3]. When every earlier token is in that set, x/t/3 at t=1..3 fires with precision 1.0, but the response looks graded and additive, not a clean boolean, so some x/t/3 steps with mixed prefixes stay silent and a d-heavy prefix gives weak firing on other tokens (e.g. d t [r], t d [1]). It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (90% of mass). It does not fire on positions 5 and later, or on outputs.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: x, 3, t; t=3: t, x, 3, r; t=2: x, t, 3, r) and the first original token (most: d, s, u, t, p, i; least: o, b, z, l); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=3 & t=5.
